text.content: These rules are not designed to simulate large-scale space battles. They are focused on emulating the movies and tv shows of the pulp action genre. Thus, the rules are focused on the perspective of the characters piloting their vehicle, often a starship.

The vehicle crew positions define what each character is using the vehicle to accomplish, particularly in stressful or dangerous situations. Each crew position has a standard and dedicated effect. The standard effect is what a character in that position can use the vehicle to do. A dedicated effect is only active if the character filling that role is filling only that role. A character that has to pilot and shoot, has their attention divided, and cannot focus as much on their role as someone solely dedicated to a single task.

A character can hold any number of crew positions at a time. As long as it makes sense, multiple characters can fill the same role. Characters can usually freely switch or add positions. However, when under pressure or in danger, a character must mark a Stress to switch or add a position.

Commander

Standard: You give orders to your crewmates. When a willing crewmember needs to add or switch a crew position while under pressure or in danger, you can mark a Stress to allow them to do so without marking Stress themselves.

Dedicated: You can lead a barrage against a target that has the Lock On condition. Mark a Stress and burn the Lock On to make an Action Roll against the target without gaining the normal d6 for burning the Lock On. On a success, choose up to two Gunners or Systems Operators on your vehicle. Each chosen character may immediately make an attack against the target or use a system against the target. If this requires a roll, it is a Reaction Roll. Damage from each weapon that hits is applied separately.

Gunner

Standard: You control a weapon mount or mounts. If you control multiple mounts, you may only choose one mount to fire when you attack.

Dedicated: If you participate in a barrage, gain the d6 for burning Lock On to your Reaction Roll attack against the barrage target.

Mechanic

Standard: You can make a Repair Action to restore the vehicle's HP or repair a damaged vehicle system.

Dedicated: You have Advantage on Action Rolls to repair the vehicle or recharge its shields while under pressure or in danger.

Pilot

Standard: You maneuver the vehicle. The vehicle's Evasion equals your Evasion, adjusted by vehicle-specific modifiers. If there are multiple pilots, use the highest Evasion among them.

Dedicated: Gain +1 to Agility or Finesse Rolls made while piloting the vehicle. You may change this choice on a rest. If there are two Dedicated Pilots, both gain this bonus.

Systems Operator

Standard: You control the vehicle’s sensors and its systems, allowing you to use the Lock On action or any other action using the ship sensors or systems.

Dedicated: Gain +1 to Knowledge or Finesse Rolls made while operating the vehicle's systems. You may change this choice on a rest. If there are two Dedicated Systems Operators, both gain this bonus.

Vehicles are attacked and suffer damage just like PCs, using Evasion to determine if an attack hits and thresholds to determine the amount of damage suffered. The vehicle has its own thresholds and marks its armor to reduce damage. When a PC vehicle marks its last hit point, roll a d6 and consult the table.

ROLL

RESULT

EFFECT

6

Glancing Hit

The vehicle clears a HP, but its systems are disrupted. Any action using the vehicle suffers disadvantage until the disruption is fixed.

5

Engine Hit

The engines are severely damaged, leaving the ship adrift in the stars. All other systems function normally.

2-4

Systems Critical

The ship loses complete power, and roll 1d3, destroying a number of systems or weapons (PC choice) equal to the number rolled.

1

Direct Hit

The ship suffers catastrophic damage. All PCs aboard make a Death Move.

Vehicles recover damage using the Tend to Wounds and Repair Armor downtime moves. When a character uses one of these these moves, they can apply the benefits to a vehicle, provided it makes sense within the fiction. A Short Rest downtime move can instead be used to repair a single damaged weapon or system. A Long Rest downtime move can be used to repair all damaged weapons and systems.

Instead of repairing the vehicle themselves, the crew may pay for professional repairs. As a guideline, it costs 1 stack of Denarii for the equivalent of a downtime move. Depending on the quality of the available facilities, this may provide the benefits of either a Short Rest or Long Rest downtime move.

The party can start with or acquire a spaceship.

Step 1: Choose Vehicle Frame

The frame defines the base size, structure, and capabilities of the ship.

Step 2: Weapons

Each vehicle has two or more vehicle weapon mounts. Choose starting vehicle weapons appropriate for the vehicle’s mounts.

If it makes sense for the story, the GM and/or players may decide not to put weapons on all mounts. They may even decide to start without weapons.

Step 3: Systems

Every frame starts with system points. The characters may spend these system points to add standard vehicle systems. Advanced vehicle systems must be gained during play.

When the PCs gain a level, their ship gains a benefit on the next long rest.

  • At levels 2, 5, 8 and 10 add a Tier Feature to the ship.

  • At levels 3, 6 and 9 the vehicle gains 1 System Point.

  • At levels 4 and 7 the ship gains 1 HP.

Weapon mounts

Vehicle weapons do not have Category and Burden like personal weapons. Instead, each weapon is has a mount type: Core, Support or Heavy. This define the type of capabilities of the weapon as well as the limitation per Weapon Mount.

On a Weapon Mount, you can either:

  • attach one Core weapon and one Support weapon.

  • attach 2 Support weapons.

  • attach one Heavy weapon.
